title: Design a News Feed / Home Timeline (Twitter/Facebook)
prompt: Design the home feed for a social network — the ranked list of posts a user sees from accounts they follow. It should load fast, stay reasonably fresh, and work for both normal users and celebrities with tens of millions of followers.
blurb: Fanout-on-write vs read, the celebrity problem, ranking, and timeline caching.

rubric.label: Requirements gathering
rubric.description: Separates functional (compose post, home feed, follow, ranking) from non-functional (fast feed load, freshness, availability, read-heavy).

rubric.label: Clarifying questions
rubric.description: Asks about scale, avg vs max follower counts, chronological vs ranked, freshness SLA, media.

rubric.label: Back-of-envelope estimations
rubric.description: Estimates read QPS, post write QPS, fanout amplification, timeline cache size, storage.

rubric.label: Fanout model
rubric.description: Fanout-on-write (push) vs fanout-on-read (pull), the tradeoffs, and the hybrid that resolves the celebrity problem.

rubric.label: API design
rubric.description: POST /post, GET /feed (cursor pagination), follow/unfollow; timeline read contract.

rubric.label: Data model
rubric.description: Posts, social graph (follows), per-user timeline cache, choice of stores.

rubric.label: High-level design
rubric.description: Write path (post → fanout → timelines) vs read path (assemble + rank + cache); where ranking sits.

rubric.label: Celebrity problem
rubric.description: Why pure push fails for high-follower accounts; hybrid push+pull merge at read time.

rubric.label: Ranking & freshness
rubric.description: Chronological vs ML-ranked feed, feature signals, candidate generation vs scoring, freshness vs cost.

rubric.label: Caching
rubric.description: Materialized timeline cache, eviction, warming inactive users lazily, stampede on hot content.

rubric.label: Scaling & bottlenecks
rubric.description: Fanout write amplification, graph store hot partitions, timeline cache memory, backfill on new follows.

rubric.label: Observability
rubric.description: Feed latency, fanout lag, cache hit ratio, freshness metrics.

functional_requirements: View a home feed of posts from followed accounts
nonfunctional_requirements: Reasonable freshness (new posts visible within seconds)
Scales to celebrity accounts with tens of millions of followers
clarifying_questions: DAU and average vs maximum follower/following counts?
Freshness SLA — must new posts appear in seconds or is minutes ok?
Media in scope, or text-only posts?
How far back does the feed need to be scrollable?
qualifying_questions: Is the feed personalized/ranked at launch or a later phase?
Do we guarantee a post from someone you follow always appears, or is best-effort ok?

estimations.traffic: 300M DAU, ~10 feed loads/user/day ≈ 3B reads/day ≈ 35K reads/s avg, 100K+/s peak
estimations.writes: ~500M posts/day ≈ 6K posts/s; each fans out to avg ~200 followers → ~1.2M timeline writes/s at avg, far more for celebrities
estimations.fanout: A 50M-follower celebrity post would be 50M timeline writes if pushed — untenable; must pull for those
estimations.cache: Materialize ~800 recent post-ids per active user; 100M active × 800 × 8B ≈ ~640GB of timeline id cache

data_model: posts(post_id PK, author_id, body, media_ref, created_at)
follows(follower_id, followee_id, created_at) PK(follower_id, followee_id) + inverse index by followee
timeline_cache: user_id → sorted list of post_ids (Redis ZSET, capped ~800)
user_features / ranking signals (separate store, batch + streaming)
reference.high_level_design: Write path: a new post is stored, then a fanout worker reads the author's follower list and pushes the post_id into each follower's materialized timeline (Redis ZSET), for non-celebrity authors. Read path: GET /feed reads the user's materialized timeline post-ids, MERGES in fresh posts pulled from the accounts they follow that are celebrities (fanout-on-read), hydrates post bodies, runs ranking to score/order, and returns a page. Ranking uses candidate generation (recent + relevant) then a scoring model on features. Inactive users are not materialized eagerly — their timeline is built lazily on first load. Media is served via CDN; only post_ids flow through fanout.

deep_dives.probe: Walk me through fanout-on-write vs fanout-on-read. For a user who follows 500 accounts and loads their feed, what does each approach cost at read and write time?
An account with 50M followers posts. Pushing to 50M timelines is impossible in real time. How does your hybrid handle this at read time, and how do you decide who is a 'celebrity'?
You move from chronological to ranked. Where does scoring happen — precompute or at read time? What features, and how do you keep p99 feed latency low with a model in the path?
Timeline caches are capped ZSETs. What's your eviction/trim policy, how do you warm a returning inactive user, and how do you avoid a stampede when a viral post drives everyone to reload?
A user follows a new account. Do you backfill that account's recent posts into their timeline immediately, and how do you bound that cost?
Posts live in your post store. How do you feed a search index and the ranking feature store off it — CDC with Debezium, or the app dual-writing to Kafka? How do you handle reordering/late events?

followup_bank.question: At what follower count does fanout-on-write stop making sense, and how do you switch that author to pull without losing consistency for their followers?
How do you classify an account as celebrity, and do you re-merge their posts at read time for every follower load?
Candidate generation vs scoring — where does each run, and how do you keep the model out of the p99 latency critical path?

followup_bank.trigger: mentions cache or redis or timeline
followup_bank.question: What's the eviction/trim policy on the timeline cache, and how do you prevent a stampede when a viral post makes everyone refresh at once?
How do you propagate post changes to search and the ranking feature store — CDC/Debezium vs dual writes — and how do you deal with out-of-order CDC events?
When someone follows a huge account, how do you avoid a fanout/backfill spike, and how is the follower list stored to make fanout fast?

scaling: Async fanout workers off a Kafka queue; shard by author or follower
Partition the social graph by user; keep an inverse index (followers-of) for fast fanout
Cap and trim per-user timeline ZSETs; lazily materialize inactive users
Hybrid push/pull to bound celebrity write amplification
Precompute ranking features in batch + streaming; score at read time with tight budgets
bottlenecks: Fanout write amplification for high-follower accounts (celebrity problem)
Timeline cache memory for hundreds of millions of users
Hot graph partitions for popular accounts
Ranking model latency in the read path
Backfill spikes when following large accounts
tradeoffs: Fanout-on-write (fast reads, huge write cost) vs fanout-on-read (cheap writes, heavy reads) — hybrid to balance
Materialize all users (memory) vs lazy materialization (first-load latency)
Chronological (cheap, predictable) vs ML-ranked (engaging, costly, complex)
Strong 'always shows every followed post' vs best-effort eventual feed
alternative_solutions: Pure pull with aggressive caching for a smaller/less read-heavy product
Author-timeline pull-merge only (no materialized home timelines) for very sparse graphs
Precomputed ranked feed batches for low-activity users, real-time merge for actives
Edge/CDN caching of hydrated feed pages for logged-out or public timelines
observability: Feed load latency percentiles and cache hit ratio
Fanout lag (post created → present in follower timelines)
Ranking scoring latency and timeout rate
Timeline cache memory and eviction rate
security: Enforce blocking/privacy at fanout and read time (don't leak blocked/private posts)
Rate-limit posting and following to curb spam
Authz on feed reads and follow actions
Abuse/spam and integrity filtering in ranking
reference.reference_answer: A strong answer identifies the feed as read-heavy and chooses a hybrid fanout: push (fanout-on-write) into materialized per-user timeline caches for normal authors, and pull (fanout-on-read) for celebrities whose posts are merged in at feed-load time — explicitly explaining why pure push breaks the celebrity case and how accounts are classified. It stores posts separately from the social graph, keeps an inverse follower index for fast fanout, caps/trims Redis timeline ZSETs, and lazily materializes inactive users. Ranking is framed as candidate-generation plus scoring with the model kept off the strict latency path via precomputed features. It proactively raises fanout write amplification, timeline cache memory, and viral-post stampede as the main bottlenecks, and covers backfill-on-follow, freshness-vs-cost, and privacy enforcement at fanout/read time.

interviewer_notes: The whole question hinges on fanout. Let them start with push (fanout-on-write) — most do — then interrupt with the celebrity problem to force the hybrid; a candidate who reaches push+pull merge unprompted is showing strong signal. Push on where ranking runs and how they keep the model out of p99. If they place a post store, fire the CDC/Debezium probe; if they add a timeline cache, fire the eviction/stampede probe. Watch for hand-waving on the inverse follower index and on backfill-on-follow. Reserve the end for freshness-vs-cost and privacy/blocking enforcement.
